summary: Keep Twitch chat independent from Channel Points APIs; support conditional reward-backed queues, local queues, free manager-initiated manual adds in either mode, and safe reward-to-manual conversion with durable redemption draining.

functionalRequirements.description: An authorized Twitch broadcaster can keep the chatbot connected to chat when Channel Points reward APIs are unavailable.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Chat readiness is independent from reward capability; runtime does not stop chat commands solely because reward capability is unavailable.

functionalRequirements.description: The streamer and currently authorized moderators can manually add a Twitch viewer to a selected queue using the existing queue add command.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: The command resolves a login to a Twitch user ID, applies current UID and duplicate rules, and creates a manual entry through the shared queue service.

functionalRequirements.description: Manual admissions do not claim a Channel Points redemption and do not create refund or fulfillment operations.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: The entry has source manual, redemptionId null, and no financial outbox task; its later lifecycle is auditable.

functionalRequirements.description: The local panel explains whether each queue uses a Twitch reward or manual-only mode and distinguishes that from chat connection.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Manual mode shows no active Twitch reward; a converted queue may display prior reward ID/origin as historical metadata. Chat and reward capability are shown separately without raw provider errors.

functionalRequirements.description: Support reward-backed (`channel_points`) and local/manual (`manual_only`) queue modes; choose bot-created reward by default or a Dashboard reward only after full lifecycle proof. Manual entry is a separate source allowed in either mode.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: New local queues have no reward_id; converted queues retain historical reward ID/origin. Manual entries in either mode create no financial operation; Dashboard reward selection requires proof of open/pause, pending/individual retrieval, reconciliation, cancel/fulfill, and safe deletion.

functionalRequirements.description: Keep the localized global ping available to streamer/moderator whenever chat is authorized, independently of reward capability.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: When chat is connected but reward APIs are unavailable, authorized ping returns existing Pong, product version, and cached Twitch latency; viewers receive no reply and no per-message Helix probe occurs.

functionalRequirements.description: Streamer/moderator can add a viewer manually and for free to any active queue, including a reward-backed queue.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: The shared queue service resolves the Twitch user and creates a manual entry without redemption ID or financial intent; archive/delete and duplicate rules still apply.

functionalRequirements.description: A reward-backed queue may transition to local/manual mode after Twitch confirms the reward pause.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Persist a recoverable transition; keep reward-backed mode on unknown/failure; after confirmation stop new reward admission, retain reward identity as history, durably cancel racing redemptions, and continue resolving already admitted redemption finance.

functionalRequirements.description: Free-form viewer chat is not an enrollment interface.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Only an explicit authorized streamer/moderator add action creates a manual entry; no chat message text is parsed as a request to join.

functionalRequirements.description: Pausing, archiving, and converting a managed queue synchronizes the Twitch reward through the documented pause control.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Send and confirm is_paused only. Twitch exposes is_in_stock in reads but does not list it as an Update Custom Reward request field; a live PATCH probe returned 200 while both response and later GET retained the existing stock value. Never claim a stock change. Reconciliation ignores stock as a writable field and confirms only after rereading the same queue version that was compared with Twitch.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Use trusted current EventSub message identity and Twitch badges for streamer/mod authorization; do not infer privilege from login text, mentions, request body, or another shared-chat channel.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: All queue mutation command tests cover trusted and untrusted authorization inputs.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Do not persist raw chat messages or invalid arguments. Manual entries never store payment receipts or claim external payment verification.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: PostgreSQL records contain only allowlisted entry/audit data.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Chat reconnect and local database restart must preserve existing queue entries and operation history.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Existing isolated PostgreSQL migrations and recovery tests pass.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Do not add Twitch scopes or network services without a documented need; keep the local-first Docker Compose model.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: No public webhook, payment integration, or additional service is required for manual-only admission.

constraints.description: The user proposes streamer/moderator manual admission by chat command as the simplest path for a channel that is ineligible for Channel Points rewards.
The product is a Twitch chatbot with a local operator panel; chat is a required operating surface.
Viewers cannot self-enroll by command or through the panel.

Bot-created rewards are the default; a Dashboard reward requires complete lifecycle proof; otherwise allow a local/manual queue. Streamer/moderator can explicitly add a viewer for free in either queue mode.
The existing integration currently stops before EventSub startup when channel eligibility is false, so chat and points lifecycle must be separated.
Do not infer reward API capability exclusively from Affiliate/Partner status or Creator Dashboard visibility; official product and Helix docs diverge.

assumptions: Existing authorized queue add command is reused rather than adding a second command syntax.
Manual admissions are FIFO in the standard lane unless an explicitly verified priority decision says otherwise; benefits such as paid priority remain outside this FND-9 scope.
Network, authentication, authorization, or server failure does not prove definitive API unavailability and never silently changes the persisted queue mode.
Dashboard rewards use Channel Points mode only if this Client ID passes the required full-lifecycle verification; otherwise offer manual_only mode without a reward.

New local queues have no reward ID. A queue converted from reward-backed mode retains prior reward ID and origin as historical metadata; local mode has no active reward management or redemption intake.
Reward-to-manual conversion is one-way in FND-9. It becomes effective only after confirmed remote pause; existing redemption operations continue, and racing redemptions receive durable cancellation.

openQuestions.question: Which roles may execute manual add: streamer and moderators, streamer only, or configurable VIPs too?
Should channels with proven reward API capability use Channel Points admission, and channels without it use manual admission?
openQuestions.status: resolved: reward-backed mode where full API capability is proven; manual-only queue where unavailable (2026-10-07)

openQuestions.question: Should new manual queue entries remain possible in a closed queue, as the existing product rule says, including in manual-only mode?
openQuestions.status: resolved by existing product rule: manual additions are allowed while closed; archived/deleting queues block them

openQuestions.question: For monetized non-Affiliate/Partner streamers, should runtime capability be determined by actual supported API operations rather than broadcasterType?
openQuestions.status: resolved through D-3 and the local-manual fallback decision (2026-10-07)

openQuestions.question: May streamer/moderator add a viewer for free after hearing a request, without the viewer issuing a command or redeeming?
openQuestions.status: resolved: yes, explicit operator action only; free-form messages do not auto-enroll (2026-10-07)

openQuestions.question: May a reward-backed queue be switched to local/manual mode, and what happens to pending redemptions?
openQuestions.status: resolved: pause must be remotely confirmed; preserve/drain existing redemptions and durably cancel a redemption racing with transition (2026-10-07)

openQuestions.question: Should pausing/archiving a managed queue also mark the Twitch reward out of stock, and how should reopening affect existing Twitch-native stock limits?
openQuestions.status: resolved 2026-10-08 from current official Helix contract and an authorized idempotent live probe: pause/unpause via is_paused only; is_in_stock is read-only for this endpoint. Do not persist or restore stock snapshots.

decisions.decision: Bot-created reward is the default Channel Points mode. A Creator Dashboard reward is selectable only if the Client ID proves the complete required API lifecycle, including recovery/reconciliation, status updates, and safe deletion.
When the API cannot provide a complete reward lifecycle, allow a local/manual queue without a Twitch reward and let streamer/moderator add through the authorized command.
Check reward capability through actual API operations and distinguish available/unsupported/unknown; do not rely solely on broadcasterType. Transient errors never change queue mode.

Manual mode has no active reward lifecycle or remote open/closed state. A converted queue retains the historical reward ID/origin; archive/delete follow the existing mode-specific remote cleanup rules and preserve history.
decisions.status: derived from D-2 and existing rules; recorded 2026-10-07

decisions.decision: Streamer/moderator may explicitly add a viewer for free to any active queue; chat text itself never enrolls a viewer. Manual entries have no redemption identity or finance operation.

Allow one-way reward-backed to local/manual conversion. Keep transition pending until Twitch pause confirmation; preserve reward ID/origin as history; drain existing redemption workflows and durably cancel racing redemptions; do not delete the reward during conversion.

Pause, archive, and reward-to-manual conversion update only the documented is_paused field. is_in_stock is read from Twitch but is not writable through Update Custom Reward; no stock state is persisted or changed by this app.
